page: Amazon Web Services m6in.24xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Nitro hypervisor. The hardware profile is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor providing 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 3.5 GHz. The CPU architecture incorporates 54 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is paired with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No dedicated GPUs or local NVMe storage drives are bundled with the hardware configuration, directing persistent I/O workloads to external network-attached storage.

Network performance is a core architectural highlight, providing a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the instance showcases top-tier encryption throughput in the PassMark encryption test and strong top-25% results across PassMark CPU score, Geekbench multi-core score, and multi-core stress-ng tests. Static web serving throughput reaches 66.43 GB/sec, and memory bandwidth achieves 327.24 GB/sec for uncached read operations alongside 139.61 GB/sec for uncached writes. In-memory data store capabilities are demonstrated by Redis SET throughput measuring 90.85 million operations per second.

While parallel and multi-core processing are exceptional, single-core benchmarks such as Geekbench single-core, single-threaded gzip compression, and stress-ng single-core register in the average middle tier. Similarly, without dedicated hardware accelerators, large language model inference shows tradeoffs; processing a 70B parameter model generates 2.74 tokens per second, landing in the lower benchmark bracket despite strong prompt-processing marks on smaller models. Qualitative cost efficiency aligns best with applications requiring high network bandwidth and significant parallel compute, rather than single-threaded execution or intensive local storage requirements.

Given its massive 150 Gbps network pipe, solid memory density, and strong multi-core processing capabilities, the m6in.24xlarge is optimal for high-throughput distributed architectures. Target deployments include distributed databases, enterprise web serving, network appliances, clustered in-memory data caching, CI/CD code compilation pipelines, and heavy ETL processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m6in.24xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine optimized for high-bandwidth networking. Driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor at 3.5 GHz, the instance delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) alongside 384.0 GB of DDR4 RAM, providing a consistent 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local disk storage and discrete GPUs, relying on a 150 Gbps baseline network pipeline for I/O and interconnectivity. Benchmarks validate strong multi-core processing, exceptional PassMark encryption performance, and high memory throughput reaching 327.24 GB/sec uncached reads, though single-core metrics remain average. With Redis throughput surpassing 90 million SET operations per second and web serving measuring 66.43 GB/sec, this instance suits high-volume network applications, distributed databases, large-scale web serving, and parallel ETL workloads.
